context: Delete the `Validate Git identity is not an agent/service` step and its id: guard-agent-identity from the code-lint job in .github/workflows/pr.yml, along with whatever identity injection was added for it. Leave `$(MAKE) agent-identity-check` in the ci-lint recipe untouched. Leave guard-agent-commit-range exactly as it is. Confirm the aggregator's guard set shrinks by exactly one and that the parity test still passes. If instead the team wants a CI-side identity assertion, the only meaningful form is over the commit range, which already exists -- do not re-add a config-resolution check to CI in another shape.
description: PR #1494 wired two guards into the pr.yml lint job: guard-agent-identity (running `make agent-identity-check`) and guard-agent-commit-range (running `make agent-commit-range-check`). The first cannot do useful work in CI. agent-identity-check resolves the identity from git config, and on a GitHub Actions runner that is the RUNNER's identity, which says nothing about what the branch carries -- that limitation is precisely why the commit-range guard exists. A follow-up change then made the CI step supply a non-agent identity for the resolution check, which makes the guard structurally incapable of failing. A guard that can never fail is worse than an absent one because the lint-guard-summary aggregator reports it as coverage. Remove the CI step; keep `agent-identity-check` inside ci-lint where the resolved identity is the developer's or agent's real one and the check is meaningful; keep guard-agent-commit-range, which inspects the commits themselves and is the real merge-time control. tests/system/test_ci_lint_parity.py permits this: it asserts every CI lint-job guard command also appears in ci-lint (CI guards are a subset of ci-lint), not the converse, so a local-only guard is legal.

anti_patterns.dont: Add the removed step to EXCLUDED_STEPS in test_ci_lint_parity.py to make the test pass
anti_patterns.instead: Delete the step; the parity test needs no change because it only constrains CI guards to be a subset of ci-lint
anti_patterns.why: EXCLUDED_STEPS documents steps that are genuinely CI-only; this step is being deleted, not excluded, and a stale entry would rot into cover for a guard that stopped existing

anti_patterns.dont: Also remove agent-identity-check from the ci-lint recipe
anti_patterns.instead: Remove only the CI step; leave the ci-lint line in place
anti_patterns.why: Locally the resolved identity is the developer's or the agent's real identity, so the check is meaningful there and is a real pre-push control

anti_patterns.dont: Keep the step and silence it by injecting a known-good identity
anti_patterns.instead: Remove the CI step and rely on guard-agent-commit-range, which inspects the branch's actual commits
anti_patterns.why: That is the current state and is exactly the defect: the guard reports success unconditionally and reads as coverage in lint-guard-summary
